summary.short: Draft PRC Artificial Intelligence Law, prepared as a scholars' suggestion draft. It would regulate AI development, provision and use within the PRC and certain activities abroad affecting PRC interests, imposing duties on developers, providers and users, creating oversight bodies, and setting administrative and civil liability. Effective date is blank.
summary.long: The draft covers AI development, provision and use in the PRC, including promotion, user rights, developer and provider duties, supervision and liability. Articles 10–31 promote compute, data sharing, open source, insurance and funding. Articles 32–40 give users a right to know, explanation and refusal of solely AI-based decisions. Articles 41–48 require safety risk assessments, incident reporting, training data quality and AI content identifiers. Articles 50–57 impose registration, a designated protection officer and annual risk assessments on critical AI. Articles 58–68 create oversight departments, a coordination mechanism, a pilot regime and an expert committee. Articles 69–77 add sector rules for state organs, courts, news, medicine, social bots, biometrics, autonomous driving, social credit and AGI. Penalties include rectification, warnings, confiscation of illegal income and, for serious violations, fines up to RMB 50 million or five percent of prior-year turnover (Art. 82). Civil liability, punitive damages and foundation-model liability are addressed (Arts 85–91). Personal use, AI scientific research and free open-source AI are excluded (Art. 95). The effective date is blank (Art. 96).

notes: Scholars' draft for suggestions, not an adopted text; the enforcement date is blank (Art. 96 'on ___ (date)'). Other laws are referenced only generically ('laws and administrative regulations', 'relevant national regulations', e.g., Arts 41, 43, 49, 90); these are not coded as relations because no instrument is named. Translator brackets mark uncertain wording (e.g., '[entity]' Art. 82, '[other]' Art. 86, '[that they are indeed providers of critical AI]' Art. 53, 'social [science]' Art. 68). Art. 93 refers to 'criminal penalties' although the text contains no criminal offence provisions. Art. 82 penalty amounts are taken as written in the draft.
